question: UNESCO has sent out another warning about the state of conservation of the Doñana National Park and, in particular, about the potential impact of the new Aznalcóllar mining project (Mina Los Frailes).

The World Heritage Committee has once again voiced its concerns about the lack of sufficient information to assess the potential effects of the project and has requested a specific assessment of its potential impact, including the effects of mining waste discharge on water quality.

The project, whose environmental assessment is the responsibility of the regional government of Andalucía, involves actions that may affect water bodies and discharge into the Guadalquivir River, in an area of exceptional ecological value protected by EU legislation. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.
Has it assessed the project’s compatibility with the obligations under the Water Framework Directive, the Habitats Directive and the Birds Directive?

Does it consider that the environmental assessment conducted sufficiently guarantees that the discharges and other actions associated with the project will not damage the water bodies of the Doñana National Park or affect its protected ecosystems?

In light of the warnings issued by UNESCO, will the Commission ask the regional government of Andalusia for information on the environmental assessment and the measures taken to ensure full compliance with EU environmental law?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (6.11.2026) Without prejudice to the Commission’s role as guardian of the Treaties, it is primarily for the competent Spanish authorities to ensure compliance with the obligations arising from the relevant provisions of EU environmental law, in particular the Habitats Directive1 and the Water Framework Directive2.

Under Article 6 of the Habitats Directive, any plan or project likely to have a significant effect on a Natura 2000 site must be subject to an appropriate assessment of its implications for the site’s conservation objectives.

The competent authorities may agree to the plan or project only after having ascertained that it will not adversely affect the integrity of the site, unless the conditions for derogation under Article 6(4) are fulfilled.

In parallel, the project must also comply with the requirements of the Water Framework Directive, including the obligation to avoid deterioration in the status of water bodies and, unless the relevant conditions for an exemption are met, to ensure that the project does not compromise the achievement of the Directive’s environmental objectives.

It appears from the available information that the project has already obtained the environmental permit required under the regional legislation of Andalusia. The Commission takes note that the legality of this permit has been challenged before national courts and the proceedings are still ongoing3.

While the Commission takes note of UN Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization’s (UNESCO) concerns, its role is to ensure compliance with EU law. Matters arising solely under UNESCO procedures fall outside its remit.
1 Council Directive 92/43/EEC of 21 May 1992 on the conservation of natural habitats and of wild fauna and

flora - OJ L 206, 22.7.1992, pp. 7–50. 2 Directive 2000/60/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 23 October 2000 establishing a framework for Community action in the field of water policy - OJ L 327, 22.12.2000, pp. 1–73. 3 Procedimiento ordinario 621/2024 ante la Sección 3.ª de la Sala de lo Contencioso-Administrativo del Tribunal Superior de Justicia de Andalucía.
